rot.capablanca.ideia.ex1.e1: This position is by Capablanca, the world champion, in his book Chess Fundamentals, from 1921. Each side has two pawns, each one facing an enemy pawn.
rot.capablanca.ideia.ex1.e2: The pawns cannot advance. So the kings have a different target now: capturing an enemy pawn.
rot.capablanca.ideia.ex1.e3: Capablanca sums it up: in this position, whoever has the move wins.
rot.capablanca.ideia.ex1.e4: The targets are far from the kings. Before going for them, the king must win the fight in the centre: win the opposition.
rot.capablanca.ideia.ex1.p: White to move. Think and suggest a move, or click {verResposta}
rot.capablanca.ideia.ex1.certo: Exactly! Your king moves straight up, on the black king's file.
rot.capablanca.ideia.ex1.revela: The best is to move the king straight up, to e2, on the black king's file.
rot.capablanca.ideia.ex1.err.e1d2.1: With this move, Black finds a resource that holds the draw.
rot.capablanca.ideia.ex1.err.e1d2.2: The black king goes to d8, on your king's file, and leaves five squares between them: an odd number after its move, and Black has the opposition.
rot.capablanca.ideia.ex1.err.e1f2.1: With this move, Black finds a resource that holds the draw.
rot.capablanca.ideia.ex1.err.e1f2.2: The black king goes to f8, on your king's file, and leaves five squares between them: an odd number after its move, and Black has the opposition.
rot.capablanca.ideia.ex1.err.e1d1.1: With this move, Black finds a way to win.
rot.capablanca.ideia.ex1.err.e1d1.2: The black king advances to d7, on your king's file: five squares between them, and Black has the opposition. Now Black reaches a pawn first.
rot.capablanca.ideia.ex1.err.e1f1.1: With this move, Black finds a way to win.
rot.capablanca.ideia.ex1.err.e1f1.2: The black king advances to f7, on your king's file: five squares between them, and Black has the opposition. Now Black reaches a pawn first.
rot.capablanca.ideia.ex1.volta: Let's go back to the starting position. Suggest another move or click {verResposta}
rot.capablanca.ideia.ex1.l1: Your king went to e2. On the e-file there are five squares between the kings: an odd number, and the distant opposition is yours.
rot.capablanca.ideia.ex1.l2: The black king also advances, to e7, and stays on your king's file.
rot.capablanca.ideia.ex1.l3: You move straight up again: three squares between the kings, still odd.
rot.capablanca.ideia.ex1.l4: The black king goes to e6, so as not to let your king through.
rot.capablanca.ideia.ex1.l5: You reach e4: only e5 between the kings, the direct opposition. The black king must give way.
rot.capablanca.ideia.ex1.l6: The black king goes to f6 and guards f5, the road to the pawn on h5.
rot.capablanca.ideia.ex1.l7: You go to f4, facing it, with f5 between the kings: the direct opposition is still yours.
rot.capablanca.ideia.ex1.l8: The black king goes to g6, to guard g5 and protect the pawn on h5.
rot.capablanca.ideia.ex1.l9: And why not take the king straight to d5, towards the pawn on b5? We will see that shortly.
rot.capablanca.ideia.ex1.l10: Remember the road: first, straight up, win the opposition. Now let's see how the white king goes on.
rot.capablanca.ideia.ex1.curiosidades: José Raúl Capablanca, from Cuba, was world champion from 1921 to 1927. This position is example 27 of Chess Fundamentals, in the chapter on the opposition.
rot.capablanca.ideia.ex2.e1: We continue Capablanca's line. The black king on g6 guards the pawn on h5 and cannot leave it.
rot.capablanca.ideia.ex2.e2: The new idea is to go around: with the opposition won, pass in front of the enemy king along a neighbouring file, when it is tied to a pawn.
rot.capablanca.ideia.ex2.e3: The black king cannot protect the pawn on h5 and close your king's way at the same time.
rot.capablanca.ideia.ex2.p: White to move. Think and suggest a move, or click {verResposta}
rot.capablanca.ideia.ex2.certo: Exactly! Your king goes around along the e-file, heading for d5, c5 and the pawn on b5.
rot.capablanca.ideia.ex2.revela: The best is to go around along the e-file: the king goes to e5, heading for d5, c5 and the pawn on b5.
rot.capablanca.ideia.ex2.alt.f4e4.1: That wins too, but more slowly: if the black king goes back to f6, your king goes back to f4, facing it, before going around.
rot.capablanca.ideia.ex2.alt.f4e4.2: Now let's go to the main line.
rot.capablanca.ideia.ex2.err.f4e3.1: With this move, Black finds a resource that holds the draw.
rot.capablanca.ideia.ex2.err.f4e3.2: The black king goes to f5, on the way to g4 and the pawn on h4.
rot.capablanca.ideia.ex2.err.f4g3.1: With this move, Black finds a resource that holds the draw.
rot.capablanca.ideia.ex2.err.f4g3.2: The black king goes to f5 and heads for the pawn on b4, while your king is far from it.
rot.capablanca.ideia.ex2.err.f4f3.1: With this move, Black finds a way to win.
rot.capablanca.ideia.ex2.err.f4f3.2: The black king goes to f5, facing yours, with f4 between them: Black has the direct opposition.
rot.capablanca.ideia.ex2.volta: Let's go back to the starting position. Suggest another move or click {verResposta}
rot.capablanca.ideia.ex2.l1: Your king passes along the e-file. The black king cannot go to f5, next to your king, nor to g5, guarded by the pawn on h4.
rot.capablanca.ideia.ex2.l2: The black king goes to g7, from where it can still return to g6 and guard the pawn on h5.
rot.capablanca.ideia.ex2.l3: You carry on to d5, on the way to c5 and the pawn on b5.
rot.capablanca.ideia.ex2.l4: The black king comes back to f6, trying to reach the pawn on b5 in time.
rot.capablanca.ideia.ex2.l5: Your king goes to c5, next to the pawn on b5.
rot.capablanca.ideia.ex2.l6: The black king runs back, but it arrives too late: your king captures the pawn on b5 in a single move, and the black king is still several moves away from the pawn on b4.
rot.capablanca.ideia.ex2.l7: Your king captures the pawn on b5. Now White is a pawn up.
rot.capablanca.ideia.ex2.l8: Your king steps out of the pawn's way, and it advances. The black king goes after the pawn on h4.
rot.capablanca.ideia.ex2.l9: The black king captures the pawn on h4, but too late: your pawn promotes.
rot.capablanca.ideia.ex2.l10: Let's go back to the starting position.
rot.capablanca.ideia.ex2.l11: To sum up: tied to the pawn on h5, the black king cannot close the way. Your king goes around along the e-file and captures the pawn on b5.
rot.capablanca.ideia.ex2.ponte: Now let us see two lines: going around along the g-file, and going around too early.
rot.capablanca.demos.outroLado.1: Attack demonstration: back to Capablanca's line, with your king on f4. What if the black king does not protect the pawn on h5?
rot.capablanca.demos.outroLado.2: The targets are still the same: the pawns on b5 and h5.
rot.capablanca.demos.outroLado.3: The black king goes to e6, towards the pawn on b4. Your king goes along the g-file: on g5, it stands next to the pawn on h5, which the black king left.
rot.capablanca.demos.outroLado.4: The black king advances to e5, still heading for the pawn on b4, but your king captures the pawn on h5, and White is a pawn up.
rot.capablanca.demos.outroLado.5: The black king will still capture the pawn on b4, but too late: White's pawn promotes well before. The win is White's.
rot.capablanca.demos.outroLado.6: Let's go back to the starting position. Tied to one pawn or the other, the black king opens the way on one side.
rot.capablanca.demos.passar.1: Defence demonstration: now thinking from Black's side. What if, in Capablanca's line, the white king went straight to d5 instead of f4?
rot.capablanca.demos.passar.2: It went around too early, without the opposition. Count each king's moves to the enemy pawn.
rot.capablanca.demos.passar.3: Your king goes to f5, heading for g4 and the pawn on h4; the white king goes to c5, heading for the pawn on b5.
rot.capablanca.demos.passar.4: Your king goes to g4, next to the pawn on h4, and the white king captures the pawn on b5.
rot.capablanca.demos.passar.5: And your king captures the pawn on h4.
rot.capablanca.demos.passar.6: Count the tempi: each king spends one move to get out in front of its own pawn, and each pawn needs four more to promote. Both sides make a queen, almost at the same time, and neither is left with extra material: it is a draw.
rot.capablanca.demos.passar.7: That is why, in the main line, the white king went to f4: first win the opposition, and only then go around.
rot.capablanca.demos.passar.ponte: Your turn: two attacks, one with White and one with Black. Before each move, count the squares between the kings.
rot.capablanca.pratica.colunas.v1.err.d2: On e3, your king leaves the black king's file: the kings are not left an odd number of squares apart, and the win slips away. Each king captures a pawn: it is a draw.
On c3, your king also leaves the black king's file: the count is not in your favour, and the win slips away. Each king captures a pawn: it is a draw.
rot.capablanca.pratica.colunas.v2.err.d3: On e4, your king leaves the black king's file instead of facing it, and the win slips away: it is a draw.
On c4, your king moves away from the black king's file and opens the way to the other side for it: each king captures a pawn, and it is a draw.
rot.capablanca.pratica.colunas.v3.err.d4: On c5, your king heads for the pawn on a5 but goes around too early, before winning the opposition: each side captures a pawn, and it is a draw.
On c4, your king retreats and leaves the e5 square free for the black king: without the opposition, each side captures a pawn, and it is a draw.
rot.capablanca.pratica.colunas.v4.err.e4: On f3, your king retreats and gives the e5 square back to the black king: it is a draw. Look at which square the pawn on g5 watches.
rot.capablanca.pratica.colunas.enunciado: Play White and find the best move.
rot.capablanca.pratica.colunas.err.d1c2: That move lets the win slip away: your king leaves the black king's file, and Black takes the opposition.
rot.capablanca.pratica.colunas.err.d1e2: That move lets the win slip away: your king leaves the black king's file, and Black takes the opposition.
rot.capablanca.pratica.colunas.err.d1c1: That move loses: Black brings the king to your king's file, leaves five squares between them and keeps the opposition.
rot.capablanca.pratica.colunas.err.d1e1: That move loses: Black brings the king to your king's file, leaves five squares between them and keeps the opposition.
rot.capablanca.pratica.colunas.fim: Your king advanced along the black king's file and, since the pawn on g5 watches f4, went around at once along the d-file, towards the pawn on a5. The black king cannot guard both pawns.
rot.capablanca.pratica.pretas.v1.err.f7e: On e6, your king leaves the white king's file: the kings are not left an odd number of squares apart, and the win slips away.
rot.capablanca.pratica.pretas.v1.err.f7g: On g6, your king moves away from the centre, where the kings fight for the way through, and the win slips away.
rot.capablanca.pratica.pretas.v2.err.f6e: On e5, your king leaves the white king's file instead of facing it on f5, and the win slips away.
rot.capablanca.pratica.pretas.enunciado: Play Black and find the best move.
rot.capablanca.pratica.pretas.err.f8e7: That move lets the win slip away: your king leaves the white king's file and does not win the opposition.
rot.capablanca.pratica.pretas.err.f8g7: That move lets the win slip away: your king leaves the white king's file and does not win the opposition.
rot.capablanca.pratica.pretas.err.f8e8: That move loses: your king goes to the side and loses time, and White wins the fight in the centre.
rot.capablanca.pratica.pretas.err.f8g8: That move loses: your king goes to the side and loses time, and White wins the fight in the centre.
rot.capablanca.pratica.pretas.fim: Your king advanced along the white king's file until it gave up the file; then it went to one of the pawns, and the white king cannot guard both.
